mfg1-mechanical-lesson-064.title: Check grounding and safe isolation to prevent secondary harm
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-064.objective: Explain protection during leakage faults and why not to approach during inspection or rescue.

paragraphs.title: Understand the protective function
paragraphs.text: Grounding is part of an equipment protection system and affects current paths during faults such as leakage. Where a grounding conductor is specified, check its connection and report defects. Do not describe grounding as preventing leakage itself or removing every electric-shock hazard.

paragraphs.title: A switch position alone does not prove safety
paragraphs.text: Cleaning and repair require the equipment-specific procedures for stopping, isolation, residual energy and prevention of restart. Some devices are unplugged; other installations need different isolation and verification. Do not touch electrical wiring without the necessary qualifications and authorization, or omit safety checks on your own.

paragraphs.title: Do not touch a person receiving a shock directly
paragraphs.text: If a coworker may be receiving an electric shock, do not pull them by hand and expose yourself to shock too. Make the possible report and stop operation from a safe position, then follow emergency medical and workplace procedures. Do not approach an unknown energized state or assume a conveniently available stick is safe for a rescue attempt.

terms.meaning: Connecting electrical equipment to earth for protection.
A fault where current flows outside its intended path.
Disconnecting a power supply or similar connection.
Further harm occurring during rescue or a related response.

safety: Do not contact people or equipment whose energized state is unknown. Isolation and rescue require the specified authority and procedures.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-064.summary: Grounding is one protective measure. A stopped indication alone does not establish safety, and rescue must avoid secondary harm.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-065.title: Match the roles of motors, transformers and circuit breakers
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-065.objective: Distinguish conversion into motion, voltage transformation and overcurrent interruption when reporting abnormalities.

paragraphs.title: Driving equipment and voltage-changing equipment
paragraphs.text: A motor converts electrical energy into mechanical power to drive conveyors, pumps and similar equipment. A transformer changes voltage in suitable AC circuits and related applications. Neither is suitable for use merely because wires can be connected; check ratings and equipment requirements.

paragraphs.title: Check why protection operated
paragraphs.text: A circuit breaker provides protection by interrupting a circuit for overcurrent or other faults, depending on its type. Tripping alone does not identify the fault location. Do not repeatedly reset it to continue operation. Report the equipment number, stop time and conditions, and obtain the responsible person’s check before restarting.

paragraphs.title: A name is different from applicability
paragraphs.text: Apply JIS and other standards or equipment requirements after checking their target and edition. Motors with the same general name can differ in ratings and structure. A conformity marking does not permit improper use or unconfirmed replacement.

terms.meaning: Equipment converting electricity into mechanical power.
Equipment changing voltage in a suitable circuit.
A protective device that interrupts a circuit during a fault.
Current exceeding the permitted value.

safety: Do not disable protection, repeatedly reset or replace parts on your own judgment.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-065.summary: Motion, voltage and protection are different functions. Check ratings and specifications, and report abnormalities.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-066.title: Choose conductors, insulators and semiconductors with conditions in mind
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-066.objective: Distinguish ease of conduction from temperature, light and other conditions; a material name alone does not guarantee safety.

paragraphs.title: Where current should pass
paragraphs.text: Metals such as copper and aluminum conduct readily and are used in wiring. Good conductivity alone does not establish component suitability: check the required cross-section, temperature, connections and specifications. Do not substitute a similarly colored material without authorization.

paragraphs.title: Where current should not pass
paragraphs.text: Rubber, plastics, glass and ceramics are examples of insulating materials. Their performance has limits depending on contamination, damage, temperature, voltage and other conditions. Do not assume every plastic product is protective equipment for electrical work.

paragraphs.title: Use properties that depend on conditions
paragraphs.text: Semiconductors are materials whose electrical properties under conditions such as heat and light are put to use in diodes, transistors and related parts. The term does not mean a simple mixture of a conductor and an insulator. Select according to the purpose and specified component.

terms.meaning: A material through which electricity passes readily.
A material that resists conduction under specified conditions.
A material whose condition-dependent electrical properties are utilized.
Ease of conducting electricity.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-066.summary: Check the material role and conditions. The word “insulating” does not promise unlimited safety.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-067.title: Separate resistor and capacitor functions from residual-energy hazards
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-067.objective: Explain the difference between current control and heating, and temporary storage and release.

paragraphs.title: A resistor also produces heat
paragraphs.text: A resistor helps control circuit current and also converts electrical energy into heat. Use components that meet the required ratings as well as the resistance value. Do not decide that a smaller part is an acceptable replacement; report unusual heat or discoloration.

paragraphs.title: A capacitor stores temporarily
paragraphs.text: A capacitor uses the ability to temporarily store and release charge and related energy. Applications include voltage stabilization, noise suppression and flashes. Do not describe it as the same mechanism as a resistor or battery. Check the circuit symbol and component specifications.

paragraphs.title: Some parts remain unsafe to touch after stopping
paragraphs.text: Stored energy may remain even after the supply is switched off. Appearance alone does not prove discharge is complete. Leave the prescribed verification and handling to the responsible personnel. Study the functions using paper diagrams; do not experiment by applying tools to terminals.

terms.meaning: A component using resistance for current control and related purposes.
A component temporarily storing charge and related quantities.
Keeping something stored.
Sending what was stored outwards.

safety: Do not short terminals with hands or tools. Residual-energy checks belong to the designated personnel and procedure.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-067.summary: Resistors and capacitors have different functions. Stopping does not necessarily remove stored energy.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-068.title: Distinguish diodes and transistors by their circuit roles
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-068.objective: Explain one-direction conduction, light emission, amplification and switching separately.

paragraphs.title: One-direction conduction
paragraphs.text: A diode primarily conducts in one direction under suitable conditions. An LED is a member of this family that emits light when current flows. This does not mean it may be connected without checking direction and ratings, or used without limits in reverse.

paragraphs.title: Signal control
paragraphs.text: A transistor is used to amplify small signals or control current on and off. Do not treat it simply as another part that only passes current one way. Match the circuit role, specified component and terminal identification.

paragraphs.title: Do not decide interchangeability by appearance
paragraphs.text: Two components with similar shapes are not necessarily identical. Check the part numbers and drawing requirements, and report unreadable markings or unknown terminals. Classify functions using paper examples rather than energizing an unknown part to see whether it lights.

terms.meaning: A component primarily conducting one way under suitable conditions.
A diode that emits light with current.
A semiconductor component used for amplification, switching and related functions.
A point for connecting a component or circuit.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-068.summary: Check function, part number and terminals together. Similar appearance alone is not grounds for substitution.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-069.title: Manage the two exam sections’ times and pass conditions separately
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-069.objective: Distinguish theory true/false questions from practical judgment questions, and plan study to meet both conditions.

paragraphs.title: Practice the formats separately
paragraphs.text: The referenced exam overview specifies CBT, with 30 theory true/false questions and 10 practical multiple-choice questions assessing judgment, planning and related skills. Despite the name “practical,” this format is different from operating an actual machine. This app’s mock exams are independently authored, not reproductions of questions that actually appeared.

paragraphs.title: Separate time and results
paragraphs.text: The source gives 40 minutes for theory and 40 minutes for practical, with pass standards of at least 65% and 60% respectively. A combined average alone does not establish a pass. Where this app gives equal weight to each practice item, it requires at least 20 correct theory answers and 6 correct practical answers independently. This does not guarantee any undisclosed official item weighting.

paragraphs.title: Check current organizer guidance for eligibility
paragraphs.text: The overview is information at the time recorded in the source. It says Japanese kanji receive furigana, but current organizer guidance must be checked for application, permitted belongings, eligibility and related rules. Passing a mock is not treated as automatically obtaining a qualification or work authorization.

terms.meaning: An examination delivered using a computer.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-070.title: Check work scope and study methods, and protect exam fairness
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-070.objective: Explain example work in the category, reading technical terms and sentence endings, and handling exam information.

paragraphs.title: The category name alone does not limit the work
paragraphs.text: The source lists many examples in the machining and metalworking category: casting, forging, cutting, sheet metal, maintenance, inspection, assembly, molding, painting, packaging, heat treatment, rolling and extrusion. Experience in one process does not authorize every type of work. Check the assigned job and required training.

paragraphs.title: Check words and sentence endings
paragraphs.text: Learn technical terms with their targets and situations, not just word translations. Ask the instructor a specific question about unfamiliar language and reread it. Practice reading to the end of phrases such as “may do” and “must not do,” without dropping negation or conditions from the judgment.

paragraphs.title: Do not take official exam questions away
paragraphs.text: The source warns against taking out questions or answers seen in the actual exam, or sharing them through public or private channels. Use independently created general examples in study groups; do not collect or recreate actual exam content. Follow the organizer’s guidance on misconduct and the detailed rules for exam day.

terms.meaning: The range of tasks covered by assigned work.
Language used in a particular field.
The final part of a sentence.
Being fair and free of misconduct.
